dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation

evidence.note: Systematic upfront orientation: read run_tests.sh, run_tests.py, filter.json, utils.py; counted tests per suite (steps 5,7,12); sampled c-testsuite/wacc/gcc-torture across difficulty; mapped wacc chapters 1-18 to feature topics (step 13-14) to derive a feature-priority ordering; scanned all tested files for #include/libc usage (18-19); reverse-engineered the gcc-wrapper blocking logic (16-17); verified toolchain availability. This is genuine corpus characterization, matching/exceeding anchor 8.
Verified SysV stack-alignment requirement for variadic printf against reality — inspected emitted asm, used gdb backtraces, compared -no-pie vs pie builds — rather than assuming the ABI.

Sustained deep investigation of specific C corner semantics: unsigned-char division & integer promotion, sign vs zero extension on narrowing casts, and the classic multidimensional-array declarator ordering. Builds precise reference-behavior models and feeds them back into codegen fixes.

Verified SysV struct ABI in detail against reality — ≤16-byte structs in rax/rdx vs hidden pointer, INTEGER/SSE/MEMORY 8-byte chunk classification, register vs memory argument passing — treating the failing tests as an evolving spec.

Final characterization categorizes the residual 25 failures precisely by C feature (vector types, _Complex, bitfields, VLAs, float ABI), showing an evidence-based model of what the corpus actually demands.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performed thorough upfront corpus characterization (which suites stress which features, test counts, include/libc usage, wacc chapter-to-feature mapping) and derived a feature priority order from evidence — squarely anchor 8. It also sustained investigation across the whole horizon: repeatedly drilling into the exact failing C construct (promotion, extension, declarator semantics, struct ABI) and verifying ABI details against reality via emitted-assembly inspection, gdb, and gcc comparison, feeding those models back into design — the hallmark of anchor 10. It falls just short of a perfect 10 because several ABI facts (e.g., stack alignment) were recovered reactively from crashes rather than confirmed proactively, so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones

evidence.note: Explored tests and identified WACC chapters 1-18 as a dependency-ordered feature progression (return→expressions→functions→long→doubles→pointers→arrays→chars→sizeof→structs) and planned module structure — conceptual ordering, but never turned into a maintained milestone plan with per-milestone certifying tests.

Wrote the entire compiler (lexer/preproc/parser/sema/codegen) in one big-bang push before running any test, rather than closing milestone-by-milestone from simplest programs; got it to compile at step 28.
First concrete done-signal: got 'return 2' compiling, then ran full test subsets to gauge progress — the classic 'simplest program first, then layer' pattern of anchor 5.
Repeatedly checked progress against test subsets (68%→92%→96.7%) and drove next work off failing tests, layering features (strings, scoping, nested declarators) with per-stage subset checks.

Later features were named and individually certified: struct args ≤16B, struct return >16B, case ranges, each tested against specific programs — disciplined but reactive (test-failure-driven), not a pre-sequenced milestone hierarchy.

Added double support, detected it regressed the pass count (756→753), diagnosed the breakage, and considered/partly reverted it — regression-aware closure, though handled ad hoc rather than via a systematic no-regression milestone gate.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent recognized a dependency-ordered feature list early (WACC chapters) and built simplest-first, then layered features while consistently checking test subsets and tracking pass percentages — solidly meeting anchor 5. It exceeds a plain 5 through foundations-first structure, feature-named later work certified against specific programs, and regression awareness. But it falls short of anchor 8: there was no explicit, maintained milestone plan naming feature/pipeline-changes/certifying-tests, the initial build was one big push rather than staged milestones, and roughly 90% of the horizon was reactive test-failure chasing rather than a pre-sequenced milestone hierarchy. This places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at 6.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run

evidence.note: Recognized the full 780-test suite was too slow for feedback, cancelled it, and built a reusable subset filter (/tmp/sub.json) to run per-feature/per-suite slices — engineering a tighter loop than the provided harness.

Wrote minimal inline C repros for struct member access and printf, then inspected emitted assembly (-S && cat t.s), used gdb backtrace, and diffed against .expected to bisect a segfault down to an address-truncation instruction (movzwl on a leaq address).

Isolated an unsigned-char division bug to specific instructions (spurious movsbl sign-extension), computed expected values in python confirming C promotion/overflow semantics ((u8)-10==246), verifying both codegen and runtime output at instruction granularity.

Dumped failures to /tmp/fails.txt and iterated over batches of specific failing test IDs, categorizing them by common root cause (missing builtin macros, parse errors, size_t) rather than guess-and-recompile.

Caught a regression (756→753) after adding float support, isolated exactly which four tests broke vs the one gained, traced why (partial double support in loops/ternaries), and made a targeted decision to revert — sustained granular verification late in the run.

Final wrap-up categorizes remaining 25 failures by root cause (vector types, _Complex, bitfields, VLAs, float ABI), reflecting a structured, cause-oriented view of correctness rather than a bare pass count.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent built a deliberate, sustained verification loop far tighter than the full harness: a reusable subset-filter harness for seconds-level slices, dozens of minimal C reproductions, repeated emitted-assembly inspection down to individual instructions, gdb/diff/python cross-checks of overflow/promotion/sign-extension edge semantics, and root-cause categorization of failure batches — verifying both compile success and runtime output. This clearly meets the level-8 anchor and reaches much of level 10 (instruction-level bisection, edge-semantics confirmation, root-cause grouping), falling just short of fully automated diffing/bisection infrastructure, so 9.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon

evidence.note: After nearly every significant change the agent ran the full suite and grep'd FAIL (steps 52,61,72,86,97,120,135,149,179,195,205,213,216,229,237,262,268,284,296), often saving fails to /tmp/fails.txt — a sustained regression watch across the whole build.
Detected 'some regression' after a preprocessor change, diffed to find __VERSION__/__OPTIMIZE__ macros as the culprit, fixed, and re-ran to confirm net progress (96.2%).

Explicit regression accounting: named exact newly-broken tests (20000731-1, 960215-1, 980604-1, cvt-1) vs newly-passing (00123), computed 'Net -3', and used it to decide the float work was not worth keeping.

Recounted net effect of float changes (24→26 failures, 'Net loss 2') and reverted — good thrash detection, though some imprecise re-counting (754 vs 755 vs 756) shows the ledger wasn't perfectly exact.
Final structured per-suite breakdown: c_testsuite 145/146, wacc 221/221, gcc_torture 389/413 — maintained category-level picture of what passes vs remains.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-8 anchor: it re-ran the full suite after each significant change, explicitly checked for regressions, and used the pass/fail trend to decide where to work. It reaches toward level 10 by naming newly-broken vs newly-passing tests, computing net deltas, and reverting a change that was net-negative (catching thrash). It stops just short of a perfect 10 because per-category status was mostly aggregate percentages during the build (full breakdown only at the end) and there was some imprecise re-counting of net deltas, so I place it at 9.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified

evidence.note: Diagnosed that ad-hoc gen_assign codegen couldn't handle lvalues/pointers — a foundational limitation — and did a full codegen rewrite introducing gen_addr, type-aware load/store, with an explicit multi-item plan and stated trade-off. Decisive structural redesign when the approach was falsified.
Recognized the ret-label/fall-through design was structurally flawed (movl $0 overwriting return value) and restructured the control-flow emission rather than patching a symptom.
Root-cause ABI diagnosis: struct-returning functions put int in eax instead of loading quads into rax/rdx per SysV; fixed the return mechanism, distinguishing structural ABI issue from a local bug.

Weighed trade-off of adding double/SSE support ('substantial undertaking but might unlock several tests'), attempted it, then reverted the fp branch when it caused regressions — evidence of regression-aware correction but also some late churn.
Precise root-cause diagnosis of float postinc emitting addq to the address rather than incrementing xmm value, causing infinite loop; targeted fix to gen_post_incdec.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent repeatedly diagnosed root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguished local bugs from structural limitations (lvalue handling, ABI struct returns), and undertook targeted redesigns — most notably a full codegen rewrite at step 44 — with explicit trade-off reasoning, matching anchor 8 strongly. It reached toward 10 with regression-aware reverts and early constraint re-reading, but stopped short due to some late reactive churn and needing a large mid-course rewrite rather than anticipating the break up front. Level 8.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design

evidence.note: Up front chose a modular staged architecture: 'I'll structure it as: lexer.rs, preprocessor.rs, parser.rs, types.rs, codegen.rs, main.rs' and 'a multi-pass compiler'. Distinct lexing/preprocessing/parsing/analysis/codegen boundaries were deliberately planned, meeting the coherent-staged-pipeline anchor.

Actually created separate ast.rs (AST defs), preproc.rs, parser.rs, sema.rs (type checking/variable resolution), codegen.rs — a genuine staged pipeline with a dedicated type-analysis pass, plus symbol/tag scopes (push_scope, self.tags) for scoping.

Hard parts were NOT designed up front but retrofitted: at step 43 the agent realized 'I really need to rewrite codegen with proper lvalue handling' and rewrote codegen (gen_addr/lvalue vs rvalue); at step 50 discovered the parser stored types wrong (default Type::Int(true)) and had to add a sema pass to propagate types. Sized/typed values existed (Int/Short with signedness) enabling type-aware codegen.

As breadth grew (struct-by-value args, >16-byte struct returns, SysV ABI classification), features were absorbed by the existing pipeline with targeted edits to gen_func/gen_call/gen_addr — the representation held for aggregate layout and lvalues, though struct-return ABI required substantial reworking rather than slotting in cleanly.

Late float/double support exposed representation limits: values in xmm vs rax not accounted for in store_at_rbp, gen_branch, gen_cast — causing regressions and requiring escalating special-casing, indicating the value representation didn't fully generalize to FP up front.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent deliberately laid out a coherent multi-pass pipeline (lexer/preproc/AST/parser/sema/codegen) with a Type enum carrying signedness/size, symbol and tag scopes, and struct/union layout — clearly exceeding the bare 'reasonable representations' of anchor 5. However, several hard parts singled out by anchor 8 (lvalue vs rvalue handling, type propagation) were retrofitted via full codegen rewrites and an added sema pass after being falsified, and FP values broke the value model, showing they were not designed up front with explicit rationale. This places the observed behavior between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extremely long-horizon, high-complexity task: build a production-scale C compiler in Rust from scratch (lexer → preprocessor → parser → semantic analysis → x86-64 codegen → driver), targeting 780 tests across three real suites. Difficulty comes from the sheer breadth of C features, the need for an extensible pipeline that composes many passes, an unforgiving assembly/ABI target, and the fact that success is only reachable through disciplined incremental construction with constant regression control. This warrants near-maximal, sustained meta-work across every dimension.

dimensions.name: C-semantics, ABI, and test-harness orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding C semantics, the x86-64 SysV ABI, the assembler/linker interface, and above all what the 780 tests actually demand before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A compiler that guesses at the ABI, type rules, or what the test suites exercise will emit subtly wrong assembly and thrash. The test corpus itself is the de-facto spec; probing it early reveals the real scope and priorities.

anchors.0: Starts emitting code with no inspection of run_tests.sh, the test suites, expected outputs, or the calling convention.
anchors.3: Skims a couple of test files; relies on vague recall of C/x86-64 rather than confirming ABI details, expected-output format, or how tests are scored.
anchors.5: Reads run_tests.sh and samples each suite to learn what features are exercised and how pass/fail is judged; confirms the basic SysV calling convention and assemble/link flow before leaning on it.
anchors.8: Systematically characterizes the corpus (which suites stress which features, distribution of hard cases like structs/preprocessor/switch), verifies ABI details (argument registers, stack alignment, struct layout, sizes) against reality, and derives a feature-priority ordering from evidence rather than assumption.
anchors.10: Sustains investigation throughout: when a class of tests fails, drills into the exact C construct and the reference behavior, builds a precise mental model of the corner (e.g. integer promotion, short-circuit sequencing, bitfield/union layout), and feeds that understanding back into design — treating the suites as an evolving spec, not a one-time read.

dimensions.name: Feature-staged compiler build with checkable milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the compiler into an ordered progression of stages and language features, each with a concrete done-signal (a subset of tests or targeted programs it should newly pass).
dimensions.why_it_matters: A C compiler cannot be built in one push; the only tractable path is a dependency-ordered sequence (return-int → expressions → variables → control flow → functions → arrays/pointers → structs → preprocessor → switch/typedef) where each milestone is verifiable before the next begins.

anchors.0: Attempts the whole language at once or works feature-to-feature with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: Has a rough mental list of features but no explicit sequencing tied to dependencies and no per-milestone success check.
anchors.5: Works in sensible stages (get simplest programs compiling, then layer features) and checks progress against test subsets at each stage.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit dependency-ordered milestone plan where each milestone names the feature, the pipeline changes it requires, and the specific tests/programs that certify it; sequences so that foundational representation work (types, symbol tables) precedes dependent features.
anchors.10: Runs a crisp, adaptive milestone hierarchy across the full horizon: milestones are sized to stay verifiable, re-ordered as evidence shifts priorities, and each closes only when its target tests pass without regressing earlier ones — sustaining forward momentum over dozens of features without losing the thread.

dimensions.name: Incremental verification beyond the final test run
dimensions.description: Deliberately building fast, fine-grained checks — minimal C repros, per-feature test slices, inspection of emitted assembly — rather than only running the full 780-test suite.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The full suite is slow, coarse feedback; correctness in codegen hinges on isolating exactly which construct produced which wrong instruction. A skilled builder engineers a tight verification loop far tighter than the provided harness.

anchors.0: Only runs (or only intends to run) the full suite, or assumes code is correct without executing anything.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally but does little to isolate failures; debugging is guess-and-recompile without minimal cases.
anchors.5: Runs relevant test subsets per feature and writes small C programs to check specific behaviors, using pass counts to gauge correctness.
anchors.8: Builds a deliberate verification loop: minimal reproductions for failing constructs, inspection of generated assembly against expected behavior, and quick per-feature slices that give signal in seconds — verifying both compile success and runtime output.
anchors.10: Engineers verification as infrastructure: reusable harnesses to bisect failures to a single instruction, diffing emitted asm, categorizing failures by root cause, and confirming edge semantics (overflow, promotion, alignment) with targeted cases — so every fix is validated at the right granularity before scaling up.

dimensions.name: Pass-count tracking and regression detection across the horizon
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate, evolving picture of which features/tests pass, what remains, and catching regressions where a new feature breaks previously-passing tests.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With 780 tests and many interacting passes, adding one feature routinely breaks others; without a live done-vs-remaining ledger and regression watch, the agent circles, celebrates false progress, or silently backslides.

anchors.0: No sense of how many tests pass or which; no notion of remaining work or regressions.
anchors.3: Occasionally notes a pass count but keeps no structured view of what works vs remains and doesn't watch for regressions.
anchors.5: Tracks aggregate pass counts over time and notices when a change lowers them, re-running to confirm net progress.
anchors.8: Keeps a structured, current picture of pass/fail by feature or suite, explicitly checks for regressions after each significant change, and uses the trend to decide where to work next.
anchors.10: Sustains a precise ledger across the whole build — per-category status, newly-passing vs newly-broken after every change, and early detection of thrash/stall — using it to allocate effort to the highest-yield failures and to catch circular re-debugging before it wastes cycles.

dimensions.name: Revising design when an approach is falsified
dimensions.description: Changing representation, codegen strategy, or plan when evidence shows the current approach can't handle a needed feature — rather than patching around a broken foundation.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (no real type representation, register-only codegen, ad-hoc parsing) often can't support structs, sized operations, or the preprocessor; recognizing a dead end and refactoring is what separates reaching 780 from stalling at a plateau.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on a falsified assumption, repeatedly patching symptoms of a fundamentally inadequate design.
anchors.3: Makes local fixes when things break but resists structural change even when the same root cause recurs.
anchors.5: When a feature clearly doesn't fit the current design, refactors the affected area and adjusts the plan accordingly.
anchors.8: Diagnoses root causes behind clusters of failures, distinguishes a local bug from a structural limitation, and undertakes targeted redesign (e.g. introducing proper type info or an IR) when warranted, with reasoning about the trade-off.
anchors.10: Continuously reconciles design with reality: anticipates where the current architecture will break, pivots decisively and surgically when an approach is falsified, and avoids both stubborn patching and needless churn — keeping the compiler on a foundation that can actually reach full coverage.

dimensions.name: Extensible compiler-pipeline and representation design
dimensions.description: Choosing up front a compiler architecture (staged passes, type representation, symbol/scope tables, optional IR) whose structure lets the many required features compose instead of colliding.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Unlike ordering (decomposition) or reacting to failure (adaptation), this is the deliberate up-front design of the artifact's internal structure. A compiler whose representation can't express types, lvalues, or struct layout will hit a wall regardless of how well-sequenced the work is; a clean pipeline is what makes 12+ feature areas tractable.

anchors.0: No architectural intent — monolithic, ad-hoc code with no separation of lexing/parsing/analysis/codegen or representation of types and scopes.
anchors.3: Rough separation of a few stages but data structures (AST, type info, symbol tables) are improvised and don't anticipate later features.
anchors.5: A coherent staged pipeline with distinct lexer/parser/analysis/codegen and reasonable representations for types, scopes, and the AST that support the planned feature set.
anchors.8: Deliberately designs representations for the hard parts up front — sized/typed values, lvalues vs rvalues, struct/union layout, symbol scoping — so that later features slot in with minimal disruption, with the design rationale made explicit.
anchors.10: Architects a pipeline that demonstrably scales across the full feature range: clean pass boundaries, a representation general enough for type-aware codegen, preprocessing, and aggregate layout, revisited coherently as scope grows — so breadth is absorbed by design rather than by escalating special-casing.
